subject: Recap + next steps: embeddings & rerank workload (scale, SLOs, cost)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps: embeddings & rerank workload (scale, SLOs, cost)

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap of what I heard and recommended next steps so we’re aligned. Please correct anything I got wrong.

High-level pain & goals
- Current pain: unpredictable p95 inference latency and spiky costs during marketing surges; search relevance drops when index grows and there’s concurrent rerank work.
- Primary goal: consistent rerank latency under load (success criteria below) while keeping unit cost within business targets.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Vector store: Milvus (cloud-hosted), metadata cache: Redis.
- Embeddings: single-model feed (proprietary embedder), indexed nightly; active index after filtering ~75M vectors (expected to grow to ~200M in 12–18mo).
- Query shape: mix of realtime single-query rerank and hourly batch re-score runs for analytics; bursty qps at end-of-quarter (3–4x baseline).

Success criteria (what Searchly will consider a win)
- P50 rerank latency (token generation + similarity lookup) < 40ms under baseline; p95 < 220ms under 99th percentile burst traffic.
- Throughput scaling to 2.5k qps sustained across dedicated pool during peak windows, with graceful degradation to a cheaper model fallback if capacity peaks.
- Per-1M query cost (infra + inference) below Searchly internal target (we discussed $X–$Y range; you’ll share concrete budget).

Risks & constraints
- Data residency and SOC2 evidence needed for private deployments — Searchly will require SOC2 Type II artifacts for pilot approval.
- Key rotation / KMS integration required for production later in the process.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing)
1) Data sample + query profile: Alyssa / Searchly — share a ~10k query sample + representative vectors (anonymized) and an hourly QPS profile (due: Tue 12/2).
2) Pilot plan & estimate: Laura / Redwood — run a throughput/latency lab run (Milvus-compatible config) and share a short playbook + cost estimate (attached scale_estimate_v2.xlsx). Target: report by Fri 12/6.
3) Compliance check: Karthik / Redwood & Searchly Legal — confirm SOC2 artifacts + NDAs (if needed) and DocuSign for pilot access.
4) Tech sync: 60-min deep-dive to scope batch re-score path and prefix/KV caching strategies (proposed: Wed 12/9).

Attachments: scale_estimate_v2.xlsx (initial cost/throughput scenarios), pilot_playbook.pdf (short outline).

If this recap looks right, I’ll kick off the lab run and send calendar invites for the tech sync.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Laura — this is great and captures the conversation well. A few clarifications and added context:

Clarifications
- Active index: ~75M vectors for our current production filters (we keep a cold archive that brings the full corpus to ~210M).
- Models: our embedder is an internal service; we can export vector batches but cannot share model weights.
- Query profile: baseline 300–400 qps, bursts up to 1.2k sustained and spikes at quarter close up to ~2.8k for short windows (1–2 hours).

Batch patterns
- Rerank batch jobs: nightly re-score of active users (windowed), runs in 1–2 hour windows at low priority. Realtime rerank must not interfere with these jobs.

Budgeting note
- We are aiming for infra+inference unit economics in the ballpark you mentioned earlier (rough target: <$200 per 1M rerank queries) — I’ll confirm exact number with finance tomorrow.

Compliance/NDA
- I can route a minimal NDA for the pilot through legal; they prefer DocuSign. Searchly Legal (legal@searchly.ai) is cc’d.

Next steps: I’ll upload a 10k-query anonymized sample + vector export to the Drive link you sent by EOD Tue (12/2). And yes, Wed 12/9 works for the tech sync.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Johnson
Head of Search Product, Searchly

Key mitigations I want us to consider for the pilot:
- Dedicated pool for the pilot (pin on a smaller number of quantized GPUs) to get predictable p95s during burst windows. This avoids noisy neighbor issues with Milvus peak loads.
- Use prefix/KV caching for the common heavy traffic queries (we should get the query histogram from Alyssa).
- A/B plan: start with an L2 re-ranker (lower latency, cheaper footprint) and run a small % of traffic to the higher-quality model so we can measure delta in relevance vs cost.

Action items for us:
- Karthik: draft SOC2 artifact list and KMS onboarding steps for the private pilot.
- Laura: schedule lab runs and book GPU pool; I’ll prepare an A/B measurement plan and evaluation rubric.

Ben
